source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Existential Quantifier (there exists) under 2.9, with Figure 2.8 printed beside it (PDF 32, printed 28).

blocks.text: The existential quantifier is used to indicate that a statement is true for at least one object in a set (as shown in Figure 2.8). It is denoted by the symbol “∃”. For example, “∃x, x is even” means “There exists at least one x that is even.” This quantifier is used when a condition is satisfied by some object but not necessarily all. It helps in expressing possibilities and specific examples. The existential quantifier is important for problem solving and reasoning.

blocks.alt: Two columns. Universal Quantifier: a box with the for-all symbol and x, an arrow down to For all x, P(x). Existential Quantifier: a box with the there-exists symbol and x, an arrow down to For some x, P(x).
